analysis.investment_thesis: Invicta Diagnostics shows an impressive ROCE of 46.4% and borderline acceptable earnings yield (~11%), satisfying one leg of the Magic Formula, but a suspicious 4x revenue surge in FY25 makes ROIC sustainability unverifiable. At INR 81.70 Cr market cap with only 3 years of operating history, this is far too speculative for disciplined Magic Formula investing.
key_strengths: ROCE of 46.4% is well above the 25% Magic Formula excellence threshold
Near-zero finance costs suggest capital-efficient, debt-free operations
High promoter holding (66.7%) aligns management with shareholders
key_risks: Revenue jumped 4x from INR 8 Cr (FY24) to INR 30 Cr (FY25) — origin unexplained, likely acquisition-driven not organic
Earnings yield ~11% (EBIT INR 9 Cr / EV ~INR 81.70 Cr) is below the Magic Formula's 12% attractiveness threshold
Incorporated January 2021 — only 3 years of financials, insufficient to validate sustained ROIC
red_flags: FY25 revenue spike (INR 8 Cr → INR 30 Cr) is a one-year anomaly that distorts all trailing metrics
Micro-cap at INR 81.70 Cr — Magic Formula works best on companies with sufficient scale and liquidity
P/E of 21.5x implies earnings of ~INR 3.8 Cr vs reported net profit of INR 5 Cr — data inconsistency
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: Earnings Yield = EBIT/EV = INR 9 Cr / ~INR 81.70 Cr ≈ 11%, just shy of the 12% threshold for attractiveness. ROCE of 46.4% is excellent and well above the 25% quality bar. On paper, this looks like a one-legged Magic Formula candidate — high quality but not cheap enough. The problem is that FY25's EBIT of INR 9 Cr is the only data point that matters here, and it was preceded by two years of flat INR 3 Cr operating income. That's not a durable ROIC track record; that's a single year distorting everything.

The 4x revenue jump from INR 8 Cr to INR 30 Cr in one year is the central red flag. Magic Formula discipline demands 3+ years of sustained high ROIC — Invicta has one good year on a tiny base. The company was incorporated in January 2021, making it barely 5 years old and a true micro-cap at INR 81.70 Cr. The data inconsistency between reported P/E (21.5x) and net profit (INR 5 Cr, which should give a higher P/E at this market cap) adds further uncertainty. Until the FY25 revenue surge is explained and sustained for at least 2 more years, this does not meet Magic Formula investment criteria.
